message:
Please review the following document.

<document>
Grant Application: Chilled Storage for Fresh Food Distribution
Applicant: Hollins Valley Food Bank (registered charity)
To: Ashworth Community Foundation, Community Resilience Fund (capital grants)
Amount requested: £48,600

1. About us
Hollins Valley Food Bank has provided emergency food to households in the valley since 2014. We are run by two part-time paid staff and around 70 volunteers, and we operate from a warehouse in Hollinsford and three distribution sites in Hollinsford, Brackley Bridge and Over Hollins, which open on different days of the week. Referrals come from GPs, schools, Citizens Advice and the local authority's welfare team.

2. The need
Demand has risen sharply. The number of households we supported rose from an average of 410 a week in 2023 to 620 a week in 2025, an increase of 66%. Over the same period our food donations have changed in character. Supermarket surplus schemes now offer us large volumes of fresh produce, dairy and chilled ready meals, but we have no chilled storage beyond three domestic fridges, so we currently decline around 1.2 tonnes of fresh food each week. Our parcels are therefore dominated by tinned and dried goods, and clients, referrers and our own volunteers consistently tell us that families want fresh food, particularly for children.

3. The project
We are seeking funding to:
- install a 12 cubic metre walk-in cold room at our Hollinsford warehouse;
- buy a used refrigerated van, so that chilled food can be collected from supermarket depots and taken to our four distribution sites at safe temperatures;
- upgrade the warehouse electrical supply to support the cold room.

With these in place we could accept the 1.2 tonnes a week we currently decline, about 62 tonnes a year. Using the national food-redistribution conversion of 2,380 meals per tonne, that is around 147,600 additional meals a year, at a one-off capital cost of about 33p per meal in the first year alone.

4. Budget
Item | Cost
Walk-in cold room, supply and installation | £26,400
Refrigerated van (three years old, 40,000 miles) | £18,500
Electrical supply upgrade | £3,700
Total requested | £48,600

Quotes from two suppliers were obtained for the cold room and the electrical work; the lower quote is shown in each case. The van price is from a commercial dealer and includes a 12-month warranty.

5. Running costs
We have obtained estimates for the additional running costs. The cold room will add around £4,200 a year to our electricity bill. Insurance, fuel, servicing and road tax for the van will cost around £6,800 a year. Our 2025 accounts show total income of £96,000, almost all of it restricted to food purchasing and staff costs, an unrestricted surplus of £900, and unrestricted reserves of £5,100.

6. Outcomes and monitoring
We will measure:
- tonnes of fresh and chilled food received and distributed each month;
- the proportion of parcels containing fresh produce (currently under 10%; target 80% within six months);
- client feedback through our quarterly survey.
We will report to the Foundation at six and twelve months.

7. Timetable
The cold room supplier can install within eight weeks of order. We would order on award, with the cold room and van in service by October 2026.

8. Sustainability
This is a one-off capital investment. Once installed, the cold room and van will be sustainable without further grant funding, and will serve the valley for at least ten years. Our partner supermarkets have confirmed in writing that they will continue to offer us surplus fresh food.

9. Why fund us
The Foundation's Community Resilience Fund aims to strengthen local organisations' long-term capacity to meet need. This project does exactly that: a modest capital investment that permanently transforms the quality of the food we can give to families, at a very low cost per meal.
</document>
response:
# Review: Hollins Valley Food Bank cold storage application

The case for need is strong and the budget is clear. However, a few problems could sink the application. The biggest is that the running costs aren't covered by your finances, which undermines the sustainability claim. There are also errors an assessor will spot.

## Critical issues

**1. The running costs aren't covered, and section 8 says they don't need to be.**
Section 5 gives new running costs of about **£11,000 a year** (£4,200 electricity plus £6,800 van). The same section shows an unrestricted surplus of **£900** and unrestricted reserves of **£5,100**, with almost all income restricted. On these figures you can't fund year one of operation. Section 8 then says the project "will be sustainable without further grant funding."

An assessor will put sections 5 and 8 side by side. You need a credible funding plan for the £11,000, for example:
- confirmed or likely funding sources
- a supermarket or partner contribution to collection costs
- a plan to grow unrestricted income

At the moment section 5 lists the costs and stops without saying how they will be met.

**2. The timetable is already out of date.**
Section 7 says the cold room and van will be "in service by October 2026." That date has passed. Assuming an eight-week install after award, give a revised date, or describe the timing relative to the award date.

**3. The demand increase is miscalculated.**
Going from 410 to 620 households a week is a **51% increase** (210 ÷ 410), not 66%. It's a small error, but it's in your headline evidence of need and it hurts credibility.

**4. The number of distribution sites is inconsistent.**
Section 1 lists **three** sites (Hollinsford, Brackley Bridge, Over Hollins). Section 3 says the van will serve "our **four** distribution sites." Check which is right.

## Significant gaps

**5. The cold chain at distribution sites isn't addressed.**
The cold room solves storage at the warehouse. But food goes out from sites that open on different days, and you currently have only three domestic fridges in total. The application should explain:
- how chilled food stays at safe temperatures at each site
- whether the van delivers on distribution days
- how you will handle short-dated items such as ready meals

Food safety is the obvious question an assessor will ask. It's also worth mentioning:
- your food hygiene registration
- temperature monitoring and logging
- volunteer training

**6. The cost per meal leaves out running costs.**
"About 33p per meal" is arithmetically correct (£48,600 ÷ 147,600) but counts only the capital cost. Including £11,000 of first-year running costs, it's about **40p per meal**. That is still excellent value. Showing the full figure is more credible and avoids looking selective. Sections 3 and 9 lean heavily on this number.

**7. The "at least ten years" lifespan is overstated for the van.**
That may be reasonable for the cold room. A three-year-old van would be 13 years old by then, and refrigeration units usually need major work sooner. Either limit the ten-year claim to the cold room, or acknowledge that the van will eventually need replacing.

**8. Volunteer and staff capacity isn't mentioned.**
Collecting 1.2 extra tonnes a week from supermarket depots, then sorting and distributing it, takes regular driver and volunteer time. With two part-time staff, say who will do this. Also confirm driver licensing (for example, that the van is under 3.5t so a standard car licence is enough).

## Smaller points

- **The 80% target looks ambitious.** Going from under 10% to 80% of parcels containing fresh produce within six months may be achievable. Show the reasoning: 1.2t a week across 620 households is roughly 1.9kg each. A target you clearly beat looks better than one you narrowly miss.
- **The van has only one price.** You got two quotes for the cold room and electrical work, but only one dealer price for the van. Some funders require comparable quotes for every item. Add a second quote, or explain why there isn't one.
- **Evidence should be attached.** Mention attaching the supermarkets' written confirmations (section 8) and any survey data behind "clients, referrers and our own volunteers consistently tell us" (section 2).
- **Monitoring has no baseline for client feedback.** Say what you will measure in the quarterly survey and what the current baseline is.
- **The meals-per-tonne figure needs a source.** Cite the source of the 2,380 meals per tonne figure (the WRAP/FareShare convention) so assessors can check it.

## Suggested priority

1. Fix the running-costs funding gap and revise section 8 to match. This is essential.
2. Update the timetable and correct the 66% figure and the site count.
3. Add a short paragraph on the cold chain and food safety at distribution sites.
4. Restate the cost per meal including running costs.

The underlying project is strong and good value. Fixing these points will make it much harder for an assessor to find a reason to say no.
